newsitem.title: USA: High winds fan fast-moving fires in Wash. state.
newsitem.headline: High winds fan fast-moving fires in Wash. state.

text.p: Two fast-moving fires fanned by high winds consumed more than 2,500 acres (1,000 hectares) near Spokane on Thursday and forced dozens of people from their homes.

Hundreds of firefighters from across the state, including crews of prison inmates, were called to the scene to help battle the fires near Airway Heights, about eight miles west of downtown Spokane, and Tumtum, 20 miles (30 km) to the northwest.
Winds gusting up to 30 mph (50 kph) and temperatures of up to 94 degrees (34 degrees Celsius) made conditions difficult for firefighters battling the state's first major wildfires this year.

In Tumtum, about 50 people crowded an emergency shelter after being forced from their homes by a fire that quickly burned through more than 2,000 acres (800 hectares) of sage and brush, according to the state Department of Natural Resources.
At least one home was destroyed, local media reports said.

The second fire in a mostly wooded area was estimated at 500 acres (200 hectares) and threatened several large homes. Officials warned residents to be prepared for a possible evacuation, and a second emergency shelter was opened.
State officials said they did not know what caused the fires, both of which were reported on Thursday.

State officials have dispatched 400 additional firefighters, including about 200 prison inmates, with equipment including five fixed-wing airplanes and two helicopters, a spokesman for the Department of Natural Resources said.
